sections.heading: History
sections.text:
Throughout the world, the Enfluxion and Undine Titans have inspired the many myths and legends about water-spirits which appear in the mythologies of cultures throughout the world.

Enfluxion was given to Sophie Casterwill by Teien Casterwill to help fight against Kiel and his fire-based Titans and spells. Sophie first invoked her outside the Pyramid of the Sun in Mexico where she fought against Vulcana but was defeated. [The Titan in the Temple of Sun]

Sophie invoked Enfluxion in Cortés' Vault to defend Kaioh the Tracker from Shadow Agent and hold him in a state of flux. She was defeated after attempting to defeat the mighty Conquistador left to guard the vault. [The Power of Umbra]

During the battle between the Casterwill family, Blood Spiral and Huntik Foundation at the Blood Spiral Base, Sophie invoked Enfluxion to defend her and Lok Lambert from the entourage of Silent Soldiers. She was defeated however by the Betrayer's Titan,Demigorgan who had been posing as Eathon Lambert's Holotome. [Lok and the Betrayer]

sections.heading: Abilities
sections.wikitext:
[[File:S2E38 Kiel Volcana Sophie Enfluxion.png|thumb|Enfluxion protects [[Sophie Casterwill|her Seeker]] from [[Vulcana]]'s fire attacks|177x177px]]
Enfluxion has the ability to control water and change her shape. Her offensive attack is using her arms as water cannons while she can also create a wall of water to shield her and her allies, a defensive ability that was strong enough to initially protect Sophie Casterwill from [[Vulcana]], until she found a good angle to target Enfluxion directly, sending her back to her amulet. {{source|The Titan in the Temple of Sun}} The shield was unable to withstand [[Demigorgan|Demigoran]]'s energy blast. {{source|Lok and the Betrayer}} By firing blasts of water, Enfluxion was also able to knock back a [[Shadow Agent]] and, for a short period of time, distract a [[Conquistador]] {{Source|The Power of Umbra}}.

sections.heading: Design History
sections.wikitext:
Enfluxion's initial design began as a [[Gaia-Titan]] composed of water with her arms being tendrils of water, and she was originally named "Ethereal". Her rough sketch was drawn with curved lines to represent the flow of water. In order to help distinguish her from the similar design of [[Lunar]]'s elemental form, Enfluxion was given legs that go past the knee and was sketched to more obviously be the actual body of the Titan. Lunar's elemental form, by contrast, is a humanoid aura surrounding a fairy-like Titan. Enfluxion's final art was given a transparent body to reflect her watery nature and was given a lighter cyan color to contrast Lunar's more purple and white color. {{source|Huntik.com/Secret Files|Huntik.com}} Following her card release on [[SAS-053]], Enfluxion was introduced in [[Season 2]] of the show with an overhauled design, and given the Amulet of a [[Krono-Titan]] instead of a [[Gaia-Titan]] as well as a new icon. {{Source|The Titan in the Temple of Sun}} In her new design, Enfluxion's form was no longer transparent, with her face becoming more elemental and less human, and her lower body now surrounded by a swirling vortex of water. {{Source|The Titan in the Temple of Sun}}

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.wikitext:
* Enfluxion's summoning commands are '''"Join me!"''' and '''"Protect Us!"'''. This makes Enfluxion one of the two Titans in the second season to have two different summoning commands, with the other one being [[Lindorm]].
* Enfluxion, like [[Undine]], is based off of [http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ondine_(mythology) Ondine], a water spirit that is one of the four elemental mythical creatures. Her name comes from the word “flux” which means “flow” or “change,” very appropriate for a water-themed Titan.
* Enfluxion is the first Titan to have been designed exclusively for the TCG before being introduced into the show with an overhauled look.
*Glitschka Studios' concept art for Enfluxion's TCG Icon reveals that Enfluxion was originally named '''Ethereal'''.

History
